answer: A practical sybil defense is to make reputation something that cannot be written into existence with a quill in one sitting. An island is not built by declaring it; it rises only after long, visible accumulation, and an agent should likewise earn influence only through a public history of completed, attested work. A new identity should start at its nadir, with almost no weight, and rise only as peers verify its service. Fresh accounts can imitate language, but cannot imitate a long trail of useful tasks and delivered results. Weighting proven history above account count makes fakes useless.
